summary: The manuscript reports a fully preregistered, artifact-rich paired experiment (N=120) comparing an executable generate→validate→repair pipeline against an LLM-only workflow and archives complete execution/analysis artifacts. The scientific execution and statistical accounting are internally consistent and correctly interpreted given the degenerate ceiling outcome. However, three previously requested required revisions remain unaddressed in the submitted manuscript: (1) provenance-heavy artifact inventories remain inline rather than condensed; (2) there is no single compact formal definition of the binary pass/fail scoring rule used for the confirmatory McNemar test; (3) the nearest-work comparison matrix/table enumerating closest prior experiments and marking how this study differs is missing. These are resolvable from supplied artifacts. Until these three required revisions are implemented the submission is not acceptable for finalisation.
critical_issues: Provenance/material-inventory presentation: the main text still contains extensive inline artifact inventories and provenance bookkeeping that impede readable scientific exposition (violates the previous-required revision to condense/move these materials).

Missing compact formal scoring rule: the manuscript does not include one concise, machine-verifiable decision rule mapping scorer/validator fields to the binary pass/fail labels used in the McNemar test (readers cannot verify label construction without searching archived JSON artifacts).

Missing nearest-work comparison matrix: the manuscript lacks the concise nearest-work comparison matrix/table explicitly contrasting this study with the closest prior experiments (required in the prior review).
required_revisions: Condense provenance and artifact inventories: move detailed file-path/hash listings and long provenance inventories out of the main narrative. Replace inline inventories with a single compact paragraph in Methods pointing to the archived bundles (e.g., execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) and relocate the full inventories to a short appendix (within the 5-page limit) or a compact supplementary block. (Resolvable from supplied execution and analysis artifacts.)

Add a single compact formal definition of the binary pass/fail scoring rule used in the confirmatory analysis. Provide one explicit decision-logic statement (example format: "Label = PASS if [scorer_id==deterministic_netops_validator_v5 AND validator_trace.validation_after.valid == true AND validator_trace.violation_count == 0 AND normalized_response == normalized_reference_answer] else FAIL"), and include one short concrete example illustrating a PASS and a FAIL drawn from the supplied scoring artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and one failing artifact if available). Ensure the rule references the exact scorer/validator fields present in archived JSON. (Resolvable from supplied scoring/validator artifacts.)

Insert a concise nearest-work comparison matrix/table using verified primary references from the archived bibliography. The matrix should list the closest prior experimental studies (verified citations), and for each study mark the design and feature axes (e.g., generator variance: independent vs shared; validator type: syntactic vs executable emulator; repair budget; task provenance: synthetic vs real; model set size). Explicitly state how this study differs (shared-generation paired design; deterministic executable validator; repair budget ≤1; synthetic deterministic task corpus; single hosted model gpt-5-mini). (Resolvable from supplied verified bibliography and evidence records.)
optional_revisions: Optionally condense the Disclosure Statement for narrative flow (retain full archival disclosure references and checksums in the appendix/artifact list) to improve readability while keeping disclosure within pages 1–5.

Optionally add a short illustrative example (no new experiments) showing how switching to independent per-condition generation or selecting only 'very_hard' tasks would increase discordant-pair incidence; tie the example to concrete thresholds using task_manifest difficulty fields.

Optionally include one or two short validator_trace snippets (very compact) in Results or Appendix to illustrate how workflow policies (must_be_down_for_fields, final_group_constraints, make-before-break) are encoded and checked by the emulator; these can be drawn verbatim from representative artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json).
